means: The effort to make a model or AI system behave in ways that match intended goals, constraints, and human preferences across both expected and adversarial situations.
why: A system can optimize the stated metric while violating the user's real intent, so alignment requires evaluation, oversight, and system controls as well as model training.

means: Overlap or information leakage between evaluation examples and data used to pretrain, tune, prompt, select, or otherwise improve the evaluated system.
why: Contamination can make a benchmark score reflect prior exposure rather than the ability to generalize to unseen tasks.
confusion: Contamination is broader than exact copying. Paraphrases, answer keys, benchmark metadata, and repeated prompt tuning can also leak evaluation information.
practice: Track dataset provenance, search training sources for exact and near duplicates, hold back private test cases, and refresh public evals with newly authored examples.
sources: [Investigating Data Contamination in Modern Benchmarks for Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09783)
related: Data Leakage, Data Deduplication, Eval Set, Exact Match (EM)

means: The agreement between a system's stated confidence and the observed frequency with which predictions at that confidence are correct.
why: A system can be accurate on average yet dangerously overconfident on the cases where people rely on its score.
confusion: Calibration measures confidence reliability, not overall accuracy, factuality, or reasoning quality.
practice: Bucket predictions by confidence, compare confidence with empirical accuracy, and recalibrate or abstain when the gap is unacceptable.

means: A difference between the data distribution used to build or evaluate a system and the distribution it encounters after deployment.
why: A model can pass held-out tests yet fail when users, tasks, language, tools, or operating conditions change.
confusion: Distribution shift is not always model drift. The model may be unchanged while its environment or user population changes.
practice: Define expected deployment slices, monitor performance and input characteristics by slice, and add new failures to a versioned eval set.
related: Dataset Split, Eval Set, Overfitting, Model Card

means: A versioned collection of inputs, expected properties, scoring rules, and metadata used to measure an AI system against a defined capability or risk.
why: A repeatable set turns vague quality claims into comparable evidence and catches regressions after prompts, models, tools, or retrieval change.
confusion: A development eval guides iteration, a final held-out test estimates performance after choices are fixed, and a standardized benchmark supports comparison under a shared protocol. Repeated tuning against any held-out set leaks test information and inflates results.
practice: Keep representative support questions, adversarial instructions, expected citations, and failure labels in a reviewed dataset that is separate from development examples.
related: Evaluation (Eval), Regression Test, LLM-as-a-Judge, Verification Gate

means: A defined process for measuring model or system behavior on representative tasks using explicit success criteria, data, scorers, and review procedures.
why: You cannot improve reliability if success is only a subjective impression from a few demos.
confusion: A benchmark score is one evaluation result, not a complete account of production quality.
practice: Run the same customer-support scenarios before and after changing retrieval, score correctness and citation support, and inspect failures by category.
related: Eval Set, LLM-as-a-Judge, Cost per Successful Task, Regression Test

means: A metric that counts an output as correct only when its normalized representation exactly equals an accepted reference answer.
why: It is deterministic and easy to audit for tasks with one canonical answer, but it exposes no partial credit.
confusion: A low exact-match score can reflect harmless formatting differences, while a matching string can still be unsupported or unsafe in context.
practice: Define normalization and all accepted references before evaluation, then pair exact match with task-specific checks when several outputs can be valid.
related: ROUGE, Eval Set, Structured Output, Pass@k

means: System controls that constrain inputs, tool use, outputs, permissions, and escalation. They can include schemas, policy checks, classifiers, allowlists, sandboxing, approvals, and post-action verification.
why: No single filter covers all failure modes, so controls should be layered according to risk.
confusion: Guardrails reduce risk; they do not prove that an AI system is safe.
related: Least Privilege, Approval Gate, Sandbox, Evaluation (Eval) ## H

means: Generated content that is false, unsupported by the available evidence, or inconsistent with the task's source of truth. It can arise even when the output is fluent and the model is not attempting to deceive.
why: You usually cannot inspect whether a statement existed in training data, so production checks should focus on support, correctness, and traceability.
confusion: A hallucination is an output-quality failure, not a diagnosis of model intent.
practice: Require cited evidence for factual answers and evaluate whether each citation actually supports the associated claim.

means: Giving a model, agent, tool, or user only the permissions required for the current task, for only as long as those permissions are needed.
why: Models can make mistakes or follow malicious instructions. Narrow permissions reduce the damage any one failure can cause.
confusion: Authentication proves identity. Least privilege limits what that identity can do.
practice: Give a documentation agent read access to source files and write access to one branch, but no production credentials or merge permission.
related: Sandbox, Approval Gate, Prompt Injection, Tool Contract

means: Using a language model to score, compare, classify, or critique another system's output against a rubric.
why: It can scale evaluation of qualities that are difficult to express as exact-match tests, such as clarity or instruction adherence.
confusion: A judge model is not ground truth. It can be biased by order, verbosity, style, prompt wording, or shared model failures.
practice: Give a separate evaluator model the task, candidate answer, reference evidence, and a structured rubric, then calibrate its scores against human-reviewed examples.
related: Evaluation (Eval), Eval Set, Verification Gate, Precision & Recall

means: A structured report describing a model's intended uses, evaluation conditions, performance characteristics, limitations, and relevant ethical or safety considerations.
why: It gives downstream builders context for deciding whether reported evidence applies to their users and deployment conditions.
confusion: A model card communicates evidence and limitations; it is not a certification, warranty, system threat model, or substitute for deployment-specific evaluation.
practice: Document model version, training and evaluation scope, subgroup results, known failure modes, prohibited uses, and the date of each claim.
related: Eval Set, Dataset Split, Distribution Shift, Alignment

means: Across a task set, the fraction of tasks for which at least one of k sampled candidates passes a defined correctness test.
why: It measures the value of sampling several attempts for tasks such as code generation where an automatic verifier can check each candidate.
confusion: Pass@k is not single-attempt accuracy, and a higher score can reflect a larger attempt budget rather than a better first answer.
practice: Generate candidates independently under a fixed configuration, run the same isolated tests on each, and report k with the sampling and estimator details.
sources: [Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.03374)
related: Coding Agent, Regression Test, Eval Set, Test Oracle

says: Two metrics for classification or retrieval quality.
means: Precision asks how many flagged items were correct; recall asks how many relevant items were found. When you change the decision threshold for one fixed scoring model, improving recall often lowers precision and vice versa. A better model can improve both. F1 is their harmonic mean.
confusion: The right threshold and metric depend on the cost of each error and the prevalence of the target class.

says: An adversarial instruction that redirects a model.
means: An attack or failure mode in which untrusted content influences a model to disregard intended instructions, expose data, misuse tools, or take actions outside the user's goal. The content can arrive directly from a user or indirectly through retrieved pages, files, messages, or tool output.
why: Models process instructions and data through the same language channel, so input filtering alone cannot reliably separate every malicious instruction from legitimate content.
confusion: Prompt injection is not technically the same mechanism as SQL injection, and a stronger system prompt is not a complete defense.
practice: Treat external content as untrusted, isolate it from authority-bearing instructions, minimize tool permissions, require approval for consequential writes, and verify outputs and actions.
related: Least Privilege, Sandbox, Approval Gate, Tool Contract

says: A reference-overlap metric often used for summaries.
means: A family of metrics that compares generated text with reference text using units such as n-gram overlap or longest common subsequence.
confusion: Surface overlap can miss semantic equivalence and can reward copied wording without proving factual quality.

means: A control point that blocks progress until defined evidence satisfies a correctness or quality criterion.
why: It converts a model's claim of completion into an evidence-backed decision.
confusion: Verification checks whether evidence meets criteria. Approval grants authority to proceed, even when the evidence is already known.
practice: Prevent a coding task from completing until the patch applies, scoped tests pass, forbidden files remain unchanged, and required artifacts exist.
related: Approval Gate, Regression Test, Scope Contract, Structured Output
